International Cheese Federation Member Spotlight Archive
An archive of 'Member Spotlight' articles from the International Cheese Federation website, showcasing diverse stories of members across the cheese industry. These spotlights highlight individual contributions, career paths, challenges, and engagement in areas such as advocacy, retail, distribution, quality management, and policy issues within the cheese community.

Member Spotlight 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


The member who answers every comment period 

 

A small farmstead owner rarely makes it to a conference, but has signed nearly every advocacy petition the federation has circulated this decade — and wants more members doing the same. 


Continue Reading

Member Spotlight 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


The distributor rep who still shows up to committee calls 

 

A regional sales director spends his days moving other people’s cheese, not making it — and he’s stayed on federation committee calls for years, for reasons that have less to do with sales than you’d guess. 


Continue Reading

Sep 



 


 

 

Member Spotlight 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


Four years building a case, one supplier at a time 

 

One retail member has spent four years turning a single cheese counter into a destination case, and most of that work happened one small producer relationship at a time. 


Continue Reading

Aug 



 


 

 

Member Spotlight 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


The counter clerk who became the buyer 

 

A member who started slicing wedges behind a retail counter now sets the buying list for three shops. Her route through the credential ladder says something about how careers actually bend. 


Continue Reading

Member Spotlight 

 

 

 



Yuri Lee 




 


A Jura affineur’s one week a year 

 

One of our members flies in from the Jura once a year for a single week of meetings and cave tours — and this year he arrived with more questions about the tariff line than usual.

Yuri Lee 




 


The summer side of a swab map 

 

A farmstead quality manager in the upper Midwest explains why her environmental monitoring program looks completely different in August than it did last winter.

Yuri Lee 




 


The distributor caught between two numbers 

 

A regional cheese distributor told us what it’s actually like to buy into a market this tight — where the spot price and the customer’s price expectation stopped agreeing weeks ago.

Five years of being the outside eye 

 

A food safety consultant who’s spent five years working with small creameries told us what most operators get wrong on the first draft of a plan.

The case, not the cave 

 

One of our retail members has spent years proving a cheese program lives or dies at the counter, not the make room — and summer is when that job gets hardest.

The wheel she almost didn’t enter
